statement: To legally change your name as an adult in Maine, you petition the Probate Court in the county where you live. Filing costs $75, and the court may not require public notice before approving the name change.
detail: You'll need to complete a criminal history record check as part of your petition, and the court may require you to pay for it. The court can't grant a name change if it has reason to believe you're seeking it to defraud someone or for another purpose contrary to the public interest.

source.title: Maine Revised Statutes, Title 18-C § 1-701 — Process to Change Name

statement: If your name has legally changed, Maine's Bureau of Motor Vehicles requires you to show documentation of the change — court documents, a divorce decree, or a marriage certificate — when you update your license or ID.
detail: Maine doesn't have a separate "name change" process apart from its regular licensing transactions; you show this documentation whenever you renew, replace, or apply for a license or ID.

cost.note: We couldn't find an official page stating the exact fee for a name-change reissue specifically. Call the Maine BMV to confirm the fee for your situation.

source.title: Maine Bureau of Motor Vehicles — How to Obtain a License

statement: Maine lets you self-attest to the gender designation on your driver's license or ID: male, female, or non-binary. You sign the Gender Designation Form under penalty of perjury and surrender your existing card — no court order or physician's letter is asked for.
detail: The Bureau of Motor Vehicles can only accept an original, signed form; photocopies and faxes aren't accepted.

source.title: Maine Bureau of Motor Vehicles — Gender Designation Form (MVL-20)

topic: Maine's legal authority for driver's license gender-marker changes
statement: Maine's Secretary of State says the Maine BMV does not require your gender identity to match your sex assigned at birth, and that under Maine's civil rights law, current policy allows a gender-marker change on a Maine license or ID.
detail: This guidance notes that Maine-issued licenses and IDs are governed by state law, not a federal executive order on passport sex markers — the federal order doesn't override Maine's law. It also says REAL ID compliance is unaffected, though it's unclear whether federal agencies will accept a REAL ID with an X marker.

source.title: Maine Secretary of State — Guidance about Gender Designations on Maine Driver's Licenses

statement: If you were born in Maine, you can have your birth certificate's name changed by sending an original, certified Legal Name Change court order, or a completed Request to Amend a Vital Record Application (VS-14), to Maine's Division of Data, Research and Vital Statistics. This costs $60.
detail: You'll need to show a government-issued photo ID. If a parent's legal name change should also apply to a child's birth record, the parents must also complete an Application to Correct a Vital Record in Maine (VS-7). You can submit your request in person by appointment, by mail, or online.

source.title: Maine Center for Disease Control & Prevention — Court Orders (Legal Name Changes on Vital Records)

topic: Maine birth certificate gender marker change
statement: If you were born in Maine and are 18 or older, you can change the gender marker on your birth certificate yourself — no court order and no doctor's letter needed. Complete the Application to Correct a Vital Record in Maine (VS-7), sign it in front of a notary, and send it with a $60 fee to Maine's Division of Data, Research and Vital Statistics.
detail: You can change your first and middle name on the same VS-7 application at the same time as your gender-marker change, without a court order — this is the only time Maine allows a name change without one; a separate application for that costs another $60. A replacement birth certificate is issued with your new name and sex, and the original is sealed from public inspection. Once you make this kind of change to a field, any later change to that same field needs a court order. A minor needs a parent or guardian to apply, plus a Gender Marker Change Health Care Professional Declaration from a health care provider.

cost.note: Changing your name in a separate application instead of on the same VS-7 costs another $60.

source.title: Maine Center for Disease Control & Prevention — Change the Gender Marker on Your Birth Record
